A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProDAG. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, references, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including content moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on linear and nonlinear synthetic DAGs and the Sachs flow cytometry dataset in Figures 1–3.

after.justification: V2 reports original synthetic experiments, training-time measurements, and Sachs results in Figures 1–4 and Table 1.

M1.justification: The DAG and sparsity projections, Algorithm 1, implicit gradients, joint variational objective, and nonlinear neural-network extension are retained. Revised experimental budgets and hyperparameter selection do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix E broadens both synthetic data families from exclusively positive weights sampled on [0.3, 0.7] to signed weights on [-0.7, -0.3] union [0.3, 0.7]. This changes the represented generative conditions; the Erdős–Rényi graph families and Sachs dataset remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds DiBS+ to the linear, nonlinear, and Sachs comparisons, and PC to the linear synthetic comparisons. DAGMA, DiBS, and BayesDAG are retained. PC does not participate in the nonlinear synthetic figure or Sachs table.

E3.justification: V2 adds AUROC, replaces the p=40 linear evaluation with p=100, and changes Sachs from linear models across sparsity levels to nonlinear models selected using consensus-graph sparsity. Appendix D revises ProDAG's tuning-grid maximum and reports validation selection for nonlinear DAGMA instead of revealed sparsity. It also changes posterior samples per optimization iteration from 1000 to 100 and real-data DiBS particles from 50 to 10.

E4.justification: V2 adds a training-time scaling analysis over graph sizes in Section 5.3 and Figure 1. Conversely, v1 Figure 3's analysis of Sachs performance across sparsity levels is removed and replaced by results at selected settings. No component ablations are introduced.

E5.justification: Synthetic evaluations retain averages and standard errors over ten datasets. V1's Sachs figure explicitly reports standard errors across ten random seeds; v2's replacement table reports neither uncertainty nor a run count. This establishes a loss of reporting, not that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Synthetic result curves are revised, p=40 results are replaced with p=100 results, and AUROC, additional comparator results, and runtime measurements are added. The new nonlinear Sachs table reports ProDAG SHD 20.9, F1 0.33, AUROC 0.66, and Brier score 19.3, versus DiBS's Brier score 18.5. V1 instead reports a linear Sachs sparsity sweep. Changed generation, tuning, and model settings prevent interpreting these revisions as matched performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 5.3 adds complexity reasoning based on cubic matrix inversion and quadratic backward computation. V2 also corrects the simple-directed-graph definition to permit one edge in each direction. The probability theorem, nonlinear reduction, and proofs remain; v1 Theorem 2 becomes Proposition 2 in Appendix B without substantive changes to its gradients.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: projection-induced distributions supported on DAGs, scalable variational inference, applicability to linear and nonlinear SEMs, and competitive inference. The added evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 removes Appendix F's qualifications about variational accuracy and convergence only to stationary points, and Appendix G's causal-sufficiency and expert-validation caveats, without relocating them. It adds interpretations of the runtime curve as closer to quadratic than cubic and of the Sachs comparison as demonstrating Bayesian benefits. The substantive qualifications and interpretation therefore change considerably.

D1.justification: Appendix D revises sampling and tuning instructions, adds the PC implementation link and license, and changes reported RAM from 128GB to 256GB. It removes the baseline implementation version numbers and the statement that all experiments took less than 24 hours. ProDAG's toolkit access remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Spirtes, Glymour, and Scheines (2001) for PC and discusses computational complexity relative to existing DAG learners. Section 2's research taxonomy and positioning of projection-induced distributions remain substantially unchanged; most reference edits are bibliographic formatting.

P1.justification: V2 lightly edits prose throughout, separates baseline/metric descriptions from linear and nonlinear experiments, moves the gradient statement and discussion to Appendix B, and adds a checklist. Author information and headings are updated, while the principal section sequence and most exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from one column to two columns with running headers. Synthetic plots are redesigned with four metrics and expanded legends, the linear results are separated into figures, a runtime plot is added, and the three-panel Sachs figure is replaced by a numerical table.

improvement.justification: V2 provides stronger evidence for the existing scalability and comparative-inference claims through measured runtime scaling, p=100 evaluations, additional comparators, and AUROC. These make central claims more assessable. The overall gain is limited by removal of Sachs sensitivity and seed-uncertainty reporting, explicit methodological and causal limitations, and baseline version information. Changed protocols mean that higher revised scores themselves do not establish improvement.
